newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes sharply down on technical sell-of.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes sharply down on technical sell-of.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed sharply lower on Tuesday after a technical sell-off led by NYMEX heating oil, brokers said.
Jan Brent ended 81 cents down at $23.25 a barrel, just one cent above the session low.
Dealers said that Brent's break through key support at $23.77 a barrel triggered technical selling stops.
"We broke down through support and then we just saw a continuation," said one.
Brent downside push was inspired by tumbling NYMEX futures, brokers said.
"(NYMEX) heating oil broke down through 70 cents (a gallon) and (NYMEX crude) and Brent lost 20 cents," a broker said.

Heating oil came under pressure from warmer U.S. weather forecasts. The National Weather Services six to 10 day outlook released on Monday forecast above normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
Traders said that delays to Iraqi crude exports failed to lend support to the market. A Turkish oil official said that no Iraqi oil had arrived at the Ceyhan export terminal on Tuesday.
IPE Dec gas oil earlier closed $2.75 a tonne lower at $212.75, having touched a session high of $218.50.
The front month contango closed $1 wider at $2 a tonne.
The release of European Union stock data showing a heavy build in distillate stocks helped to push gas oil off highs, brokers said.
Middle distillate stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 2.55 million barrels or 0.9 percent in November to 295.73 million barrels, the Euroilstock foundation said on Tuesday.
Distillate stocks were 770,000 barrels higher than at the end of November 1995, wiping out the year-on-year shortfall that has persisted for most of the year.
EU crude oil stocks rose 6.35 million barrels or 1.6 percent, to 405.95 million barrels, still 8.65 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, lower year-on-year.
